 Follow us on Facebook Twitter Hello Latest news Social Security’s maximum retirement benefit rises in 2027, but reaching the $5,358 monthly payment requires decades of high earnings and careful timing.
 Getty Images Social Security $5,358 Social Security checks: These are the retirees who get the maximum payment and the requirements they meet
 Greg Heilman Calum Roche twitter Update: Nov 20th, 2026 04:54 EST 0 Share facebook twitter whatsapp Make us preferred on Google According to data from the Social Security Administration (SSA) , approximately 58.1 million people received Social Security retirement benefits in October 2026, including spouses and children of retired workers, as well as the workers themselves.
 For retired workers, the average Social Security retirement benefit was approximately $2,092 per month , although the exact amount varies depending on each individual’s circumstances.
 However, the maximum monthly retirement benefit will rise to $5,358 in 2027 , provided certain requirements are met.
 How does Social Security calculate your retirement benefit?
 The two main factors that determine how much you receive are your average earnings over your career and your age when you claim benefits . The more you earn in jobs covered by Social Security, the higher your monthly retirement benefit can be. And the longer you wait to claim, the more you can receive each month, particularly if you delay beyond your full retirement age.
 The amount of earnings that counts toward the maximum benefit is adjusted annually based on changes in national wage levels. To calculate your benefit, the SSA takes an average of your earnings over the 35 highest-earning years of your career . If you worked for fewer than 35 years, the years in which you had no earnings count as zero, bringing down your average.
 How to receive the maximum Social Security retirement benefit
 If you claim retirement benefits at 62, the earliest age at which you can start receiving payments, the maximum benefit in 2027 is $3,094 a month for someone claiming at 62 and one month. However, those who put off claiming benefits receive a higher monthly payment for each year they wait, up to age 70.
 For those who wait until their full retirement age (FRA) to claim benefits, the maximum monthly benefit in 2027 is $4,188 for someone whose FRA is 67. Your FRA is 67 if you were born in 1960 or later, and progressively lower if you were born earlier.
 If you want to receive the highest possible Social Security retirement benefit, you’ll need to wait until age 70 to claim. You’ll also need a long history of earnings at or above the maximum amount of income subject to Social Security taxes, generally covering at least 35 years. In 2027, the SSA’s maximum taxable earnings limit will be $192,300, up from $184,500 in 2026.
 The maximum Social Security retirement benefit available to someone claiming at age 70 in 2027 will be $5,358 a month , equivalent to $64,296 a year, for someone who meets the earnings requirements. This amount can change each year as Social Security benefits are adjusted for inflation and earnings calculations are updated.
